quests.instruction: Two friends each have a toy they like. They agree to give each other their toy for the afternoon. What do they do?
quests.hint: Each takes the other's toy.
quests.explanation: Swap means to give something and get something else in return.
quests.funFact: Collectors often swap cards or stickers to complete a set.

quests.instruction: On the monkey bars, Ravi holds on with both hands, and his feet are off the ground. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: His body is held up by his arms.
quests.explanation: Hang means to be held up from above with nothing under you.
quests.funFact: Bats hang upside down to sleep.

quests.instruction: In a game of dodgeball, Zoe moves quickly aside so the ball misses her. What does she do?
quests.hint: She avoids something coming toward her.
quests.explanation: Dodge means to move quickly to avoid something or someone.
quests.funFact: In dodgeball, the whole game is built around dodging.

quests.instruction: To get across the stream, Max takes a big jump from one rock to another. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: It is a long, strong jump.
quests.explanation: Leap means to jump a long way or very high.
quests.funFact: A leap year has an extra day, which helps the calendar stay in step with the seasons.

quests.instruction: When the ice-cream van appears, the children rush quickly to it in a short burst of speed. What do they do?
quests.hint: They move very quickly for a short time.
quests.explanation: Dash means to run or go somewhere fast and suddenly.
quests.funFact: The hundred-metre dash is a famous short race.

quests.instruction: Noor bends her knees and lowers her body close to the ground to stay hidden during a game. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: Her body gets close to the ground.
quests.explanation: Crouch means to bend your knees and lower your body close to the ground.
quests.funFact: Cats crouch before they jump.

quests.instruction: The postman brings the letters to each house on the street. What does he do?
quests.hint: Items go from him to the door.
quests.explanation: Deliver means to take something to a person or a place.
quests.funFact: 'Deliver' also means to give a speech.

quests.instruction: Sara puts her letter into the red box so it will travel to her grandma. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: It starts its journey to someone far away.
quests.explanation: Post means to send a letter or parcel through the mail. It can also mean to put something up on a wall or a website.
quests.funFact: Britain's red post boxes have been used for well over a hundred years.

quests.instruction: At the museum, a woman walks in front of the visitors and shows them where to go. What does she do?
quests.hint: She helps people find their way.
quests.explanation: Guide means to show someone the way or help them find what they need.
quests.funFact: A guide dog helps a blind person walk safely around obstacles.

quests.instruction: A street light is broken, and the workers come with ladders to make it work again. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: They fix something broken in the community.
quests.explanation: Repair means to fix something that is damaged or not working.
quests.funFact: Repair cafés are places where volunteers help people mend broken things.

quests.instruction: In the park, Ali sees a bag of rubbish, picks it up and puts it into a bin. What does he do?
quests.hint: He lifts something from the ground.
quests.explanation: Pick up means to lift something from the ground or a surface.
quests.funFact: A park stays cleaner if everyone picks up after themselves.

quests.instruction: A child sees a broken swing at the playground and tells the park manager so it can be mended. Choose the best verb.
quests.hint: He tells somebody in charge.
quests.explanation: Report means to tell the right person about something that has happened or is wrong.
quests.funFact: Reporting a problem early can stop someone getting hurt.

quests.instruction: The doctor examines Tom's sore ear and gives him medicine. What does the doctor do?
quests.hint: She tries to make a sick person better.
quests.explanation: Treat means to try to make an ill or hurt person or animal better.
quests.funFact: 'Treat' can also mean a special gift or snack, as in 'a treat for your birthday'.

quests.instruction: A bus driver takes the passengers from the town centre to the school every morning. Which verb matches what happens?
quests.hint: He is in control of the vehicle.
quests.explanation: Drive means to control a vehicle, such as a bus, car or tractor.
quests.funFact: Some countries drive on the left side of the road and some on the right.

quests.instruction: A farmer plants rice in spring and, by autumn, he has a big harvest. What does the farmer do?
quests.hint: He looks after plants as they get bigger.
quests.explanation: Grow means to look after plants or animals so they get bigger. It can also mean to get bigger yourself.
quests.funFact: One rice plant can make hundreds of grains.

quests.instruction: At the red light, the cars all ___ and wait for the green light.
quests.hint: Their wheels do not move.
quests.explanation: Stop means to not move any more or to come to a halt.
quests.funFact: Red is used for stop signs in many countries because it can be seen from a long way off.

quests.instruction: On the school trip, the teacher tells everyone to ___ together so that nobody gets lost.
quests.hint: Think about what keeps a group in one place.
quests.explanation: Stay means to remain in the same place or with the same people. Staying together is a safety rule on trips.
quests.funFact: Teachers often count the children before and after a trip to make sure that everyone is still there.

quests.instruction: There is a wet floor in the corridor, so Priya walks around the wet part. Which verb fits the scene?
quests.hint: She keeps away from something that could cause trouble.
quests.explanation: Avoid means to keep away from something or someone to stay safe or free from trouble.
quests.funFact: Yellow signs warn people about wet floors so that they can avoid slipping.

quests.instruction: In an emergency, Rani presses the number on her phone to talk to the emergency services. What does she do?
quests.hint: She uses the numbers on the phone.
quests.explanation: Dial means to press or turn numbers on a phone to call someone.
quests.funFact: Old telephones had a round dial that you turned with your finger.

quests.instruction: The smoke alarm rings, and the family quickly goes outside by the nearest door. Choose the action word that matches.
quests.hint: They get away from the danger.
quests.explanation: Escape means to get away from a place or situation that is dangerous.
quests.funFact: Schools and offices practise fire drills so everyone knows how to escape.

quests.instruction: When an earthquake begins, children are taught to get under a strong table to protect their heads. They ___ their heads.
quests.hint: Something is placed over something else to keep it safe.
quests.explanation: Cover means to put something over another thing to protect it or hide it.
quests.funFact: 'Cover' can also mean to be enough for something: a few coins will cover the bus fare.

quests.instruction: Ben has done his homework, tidied his room and put his bag by the door. He has ___ his tasks.
quests.hint: He did everything.
quests.explanation: Finish means to complete something. Here the form 'finished' tells us that it is done.
quests.funFact: 'Finish' is the opposite of 'start' or 'begin'.

quests.instruction: Before bed, Mum chooses the time she wants to get up and puts it into her alarm clock. What does she do?
quests.hint: She makes the clock ready for a certain time.
quests.explanation: Set means to put a clock or a machine at the right time or position.
quests.funFact: You can set a table, a clock, a goal or a record.

quests.instruction: At the end of each school day, Rina puts the chairs in a straight row. Which verb describes the action?
quests.hint: She puts things in a neat order.
quests.explanation: Arrange means to put things in a neat order or plan something in advance.
quests.funFact: Flowers are arranged in a vase to look beautiful.

quests.instruction: Kofi told his friend he would be at the library at four o'clock, and he is there exactly on time. He ___ his promise.
quests.hint: He did what he said.
quests.explanation: Keep a promise means to do what you said you would do. The past of 'keep' is 'kept'.
quests.funFact: 'Keep' has many meanings: you can keep a secret, keep a pet or keep calm.

quests.instruction: Mia is in charge of her baby cousin for an afternoon and makes sure that he is safe and happy. What does she do?
quests.hint: She takes responsibility for someone.
quests.explanation: Look after means to take care of someone or something.
quests.funFact: 'Look after' is also used for pets, plants and younger brothers and sisters.

quests.instruction: Every evening, Leo goes outside with his dog and takes him around the block. What does he do with the dog?
quests.hint: He takes the dog out for exercise.
quests.explanation: Walk can mean to take an animal out for exercise: Leo walks his dog.
quests.funFact: Dogs need exercise every day, and walking is how many families give it to them.

quests.instruction: Dev comes to every class on time and sits ready to learn. He ___ school regularly.
quests.hint: He goes to it as he should.
quests.explanation: Attend means to be present at a place or an event, like a class or a party.
quests.funFact: 'Attend' also means to pay attention: attend to what the teacher says.

quests.instruction: While the teacher speaks, Aisha writes down the main points in her notebook. Which action word is being shown?
quests.hint: She records key ideas while listening.
quests.explanation: Take notes means to write down short, important points while listening or reading.
quests.funFact: Taking notes helps you remember because you have to decide what is important.

quests.instruction: When the teacher asks questions, Sam always puts up his hand and joins in the discussion. He ___ in class.
quests.hint: He takes an active part.
quests.explanation: Participate means to take an active part in something.
quests.funFact: In many schools, participation is as important as test scores.
